purpose: personal account of Alexey's historical Claude Code command and continuation-loop experiments

required_facts.fact: Alexey had tried Claude Code six months earlier, disliked its terminal experience, and preferred an IDE assistant; later he tried it again because of social media discussion.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 1-6: prior preference, renewed interest, and continued preference for Copilot are described.

required_facts.fact: Claude commands are slash commands executed in Claude Code and are defined as Markdown files in .claude/commands.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 10 and 19: command form and file location are stated.

required_facts.fact: Alexey created /kid and /parent, where one generated absurd project ideas and the other implemented them in HTML and JavaScript.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 21-23: both commands and their roles are described.

required_facts.fact: Running the pair in a loop produced more than 25 standalone projects, mostly with embedded CSS and JavaScript and no external dependencies.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 26-31: loop output, count, file form, and examples are listed.

required_facts.fact: Claude stopped after a few loop iterations, so Alexey investigated stop hooks and the Ralph Wiggum plugin.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 36-40: failed continuation and plugin discovery are described.

required_facts.fact: The prompt-hook documentation example was outdated and did not work in the experiment.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 38: the documentation problem is stated.

required_facts.fact: Alexey tested the loop on a metabolism simulator to help him understand human metabolism.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 53-55: project purpose and initial prompt are described.

required_facts.fact: The Ralph hook failed on Windows because it was implemented as a Bash command.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 58-63: Windows limitation and platform qualification are stated.

required_facts.fact: Alexey implemented a Python continuation hook controlled by continue.md and added a restart script for Claude Code errors.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 67-85: Python hook files, stop switch, and restart script are described.

required_facts.fact: After several days the generated site had many features but was incomplete, and Alexey would not let the loop run freely on real projects.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 87-91: result quality, deleted-test concern, and caution are stated.

author_attribution: Attribute all experiments, judgments, and limitations to Alexey's historical account; preserve his caution about autonomous loops.
